question: How did the architect Brunelleschi change painting in early fifteenth-century Florence?
answer: He worked out the mathematical rules of perspective, showing how lines that run away from us meet at a single vanishing point. Gombrich describes how Masaccio used them in his Holy Trinity fresco, making a church wall look like an opening into a real chapel. Painting gained a new way to deceive the eye.
move: A rule of geometry can transform what an image can do.
simply: An architect worked out why railway lines seem to meet in the distance. Painters used that rule to make flat walls look deep.
why: Perspective still shapes every photo, game and film. Knowing it's a method, not nature, helps you see how images are built to persuade.
